title: 航空流体力学A
subtitle: Aerodynamics A
keywords: Governing equation 2.Potential flow 3.Conformal transformation 4.Airfoil and wing planform
educationalGoal: Fluid dynamics is one of the major subjects in the machine and aeronautical fields. Students will learn the method of theoretical analysis of fluids using the governing equation. The goal of this subject is to understand the aerodynamic characteristics of the wings of aircraft, and to learn how to analyze the fluid around objects in irrotational ideal flow.
advice: We will learn the two-dimensional flow of incompressible, inviscid and irrotational fluids, and how to apply the theory to airplane wings. We will cover the following materials: 1. Governing equation of fluid flow 2. Velocity potential 3. Flow around a cylinder 4. Kutta-Joukowski theorem 4. Conformal transformation 5. Flow around an airfoil and thin airfoil theory 6. Aerodynamic characteristics of two-dimensional wings 7. Aerodynamic characteristics of three-dimensional wings Students must take and review notes because not everything is in the textbook.
books: Introduction to aerodynamics, Maruzen publishing, in Japanese
requiredKnowledge: Acquisition of fluid mechanics. Sufficient skill in mathematics (especially differential and integral calculations).

activityGoals.body: Be able to explain the governing equation of fluid flow.
Be able to analyze simple irrotational flow.
Be able to explain the mechanism of wing lift generation.
Be able to estimate the aerodynamic characteristics of a two-dimensional wing.
Be able to explain the aerodynamic characteristics of a three-dimensional wing.

achievementLevels.ideal: (1) Analyze simple irrotational flow by the potential theory. (2) Estimate the aerodynamic characteristics of a two-dimensional wing and explain the mechanism of wing lift generation precisely. (3) Explain the aerodynamic characteristics of a three-dimensional wing. (4) Explain the application of the aerodynamic characteristics of wings to aircraft.
achievementLevels.standard: (1) Analyze simple irrotational flow by the potential theory. (2) Estimate the aerodynamic characteristics of a two-dimensional wing and explain the mechanism of wing lift generation. (3) Explain the aerodynamic characteristics of a three-dimensional wing.

lessons.content: Review of the governing equation of fluids and analysis of complex functions
Review of velocity potential and stream function
Review of complex analysis and complex velocity potential
Review of conformal mapping and Joukowski wing
Review of Kutta-Joukowski theorem and Blasius formula (additional)
Review of the aerodynamic characteristics of an airfoil

lessons.assignments: Confirm what you learned and create an assignment report.

lessons.content: Review of the aerodynamic characteristics of a three-dimensional wing
